title: NRES-016 finite-horizon adaptive recourse protocol template
research_question: Do non-anticipative adaptive policies with explicit resource ledgers and stagewise transition ambiguity reduce service deficit and realized regret under independent shift trajectories compared with static and rolling-horizon baselines?

horizon_contract.terminal_state: all remaining service deficits, asset states, inventories, workforce and unresolved actions are recorded; no terminal resource reset
horizon_contract.replanning_rule: replan only after a new observation becomes available; preserve already consumed resources and committed actions

state_definition.semantics: separate capacity and shortfall for every service at every stage
condition, failure state, repair work in progress and expected completion
on-hand stock, committed procurement, shipment state and uncertain lead time
available staff hours, skill/role constraints and transport availability
evidence freshness, missingness, verification status and observation history

resource_ledgers.conservation_rule: opening balance minus committed and consumed spend plus observed replenishment
resource_ledgers.replenishment_semantics: credit only when an observed or scenario-realized replenishment transition occurs

resource_ledgers.conservation_rule: opening deployable hours minus allocated hours plus explicitly modelled shift/rest recovery
resource_ledgers.replenishment_semantics: future shifts enter only at their availability stage and subject to role qualification

resource_ledgers.conservation_rule: on-hand stock minus consumed items plus realized deliveries
resource_ledgers.replenishment_semantics: deliveries arrive after declared uncertain lead times

information_structure.nonanticipativity_rule: all scenario paths with identical observable histories through stage t must select the same action at t
information_structure.history_identity: canonical history key over prior observations, public evidence and prior actions; hidden future shocks and scenario labels are excluded
negative_controls: changing future disturbances cannot change earlier actions
permuting hidden scenario labels cannot change policy decisions
duplicating a path with identical observable history cannot increase independent sample count
withholding a future observation prevents its use by the current policy

allowed_action_effects: protection changes later failure probability or failure severity
repair changes recovery-time and repeat-failure transition distributions
verification changes observation quality or posterior uncertainty but not physical capacity unless specified
decision_dependent_uncertainty.causal_evidence_rule: action-dependent transitions are modelling assumptions unless supported by a separately identified causal design; never infer intervention effects from correlation alone

risk_contract.ambiguity_order: state the order of stagewise worst-case transition selection and conditional risk aggregation; freeze ambiguity sets and risk levels before confirmatory evaluation

hard_constraints: nonnegative resource ledger at every stage and every path
action feasibility for each observable information state
hard role, privacy and safety constraints are not softened into objective penalties
per-service floor constraints are reported separately at every stage

candidate_methods.description: fixed action sequence chosen before disturbances are observed
deterministic model-predictive control with re-optimization after each observation
preparation followed by one recourse stage
expected-cost multistage recourse under a frozen scenario law
non-anticipative multistage decisions under a declared uncertainty set
state/action-conditioned ambiguity sets with a declared rectangularity or coupling contract
perfect-information lower bound only; inadmissible as a deployable policy

reporting_metrics: pathwise realized cost and statewise regret
worst-case pathwise regret and nested dynamic risk bound
CVaR95 and CVaR99 with static versus nested semantics
forecast score, ambiguity coverage, radius and vacuity
hard constraint violations and infeasibility status
solve time, peak memory, optimality gap and anytime incumbent
guardrails: no real-world resource dispatch or emergency command
no legal or public-health readiness certification
no personal-suitability, political-belief or loyalty scoring
all methods share identical information sets, paths and resource constraints
publish infeasibility, timeout, vacuity, abstention and non-improvement outcomes
